title: robots.txt
content: robots.txt is a website file that tells cooperating crawlers which paths they may request.

meta.why: A rule can prevent a crawler from fetching a page you intended it to read.
meta.example: A Disallow rule for an old staging directory remains after that directory becomes a public resource library.
meta.check: Review the rules for the specific crawler and path, and coordinate changes with the person responsible for security and publishing.
meta.limitation: robots.txt is not a privacy control or a reliable removal method. A blocked URL can still appear in search, and a blocked crawler cannot read a page’s noindex tag.
